paper_title: Fusing Porphyrins and Phospholes: Synthesis and Analysis of a Phosphorus-Containing Porphyrin
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Angew Chem Int Ed - 2016 - Higashino - Fusing Porphyrins and Phospholes  Synthesis and Analysis of a Phosphorus‐Containing/auto/Angew Chem Int Ed - 2016 - Higashino - Fusing Porphyrins and Phospholes  Synthesis and Analysis of a Phosphorus‐Containing.md

knowledge_points.content: The phosphole-fused porphyrin dimer 12 is synthesized through the acid-catalyzed condensation of bis(pyrrolo)phosphole 8 and tripyrrane dicarbinol 11 using 0.4 equivalents of methanesulfonic acid (MSA) in 1,2-dichloroethane, followed by oxidation with DDQ.
knowledge_points.evidence: we finally succeeded in isolating the desired porphyrin dimer 12 in 0.7% yield upon condensation of 8 and 11 with 0.4 equiv of methanesulfonic acid (MSA) at 60 °C in 1,2-dichloroethane for 1 h followed by oxidation with 6 equiv of 2,3-dichloro-5,6-dicyanobenzoquinone (DDQ)

knowledge_points.content: X-ray crystal structure analysis of the porphyrin dimer 12 reveals two almost co-planar porphyrin macrocycles, which facilitates effective pi-conjugation across the phosphole moiety.
knowledge_points.evidence: The crystal structure of 12 revealed two almost co-planar porphyrin macrocycles, which suggests effective pi-conjugation over the two porphyrin moieties (Figure 3).

knowledge_points.content: In the solid state, the phosphole-fused porphyrin dimer 12 forms a slipped face-to-face pi-stacked dimeric structure with an intermolecular distance of approximately 3.5 Å.
knowledge_points.evidence: In the packing structure, 12 forms a face-to-face dimeric structure, in which the intermolecular distance is approximately 3.5 Å (Figure S5). Notably, this dimeric structure forms a slipped pi-pi stacked structure

knowledge_points.content: The Q band of the phosphole-fused porphyrin dimer 12 is observed at 668 nm, representing a red shift of 43 nm compared to the porphyrin monomer 13 (625 nm).
knowledge_points.evidence: The lowest-energy Q band of 12 (lambda = 668 nm) is red-shifted by Delta lambda = 43 nm relative to that of 13 (lambda = 625 nm)

knowledge_points.content: The phosphole-fused porphyrin dimer 12 exhibits high electron affinity with an estimated LUMO level of -3.61 eV, which is nearly identical to the common electron acceptor [60]PCBM (ca. -3.7 eV).
knowledge_points.evidence: the LUMO level of 12 was estimated to be -3.61 eV. [15] This value is close to that of [60]PCBM (ca. -3.7 eV, [16] a representative fullerene derivative that is used as an electron-accepting material

knowledge_points.content: The fusion of two porphyrin moieties with a phosphole ring significantly stabilizes the LUMO because the LUMO orbital is delocalized over both the porphyrin macrocycles and the phosphole ring.
knowledge_points.evidence: the LUMO of 12a is well delocalized over the two porphyrin moieties as well as the phosphole ring (Figure 5b). ... As the LUMO displays a large orbital distribution on the phosphole ring, the LUMO possesses phosphole character to a large extent.

knowledge_points.content: Flash photolysis time-resolved microwave conductivity (FP-TRMC) measurements show that the maximum transient conductivity (Phi*Sigma*mu) of the porphyrin dimer 12 is 5.5 x 10^-5 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1, which is ten times higher than that of the monomer 13.
knowledge_points.evidence: Importantly, the (Phi*Sigma*mu)max value for 12 (5.5 x 10^-5 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1) is one order of magnitude larger than that for 13 (6.5 x 10^-6 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1).

knowledge_points.content: Nucleus-independent chemical shift (NICS) calculations for the porphyrin dimer 12 show a large positive value of +8.33 ppm at the center of the phosphole ring, attributed to the double diatropic ring current effect from the adjacent porphyrin macrocycles.
knowledge_points.evidence: the NICS value at the center of the phosphole ring is +8.33 ppm. This large positive NICS value results from the double diatropic ring current effect of the two porphyrin macrocycles.

knowledge_points.content: The phosphole-fused porphyrin dimer 12 undergoes three quasi-reversible one-electron reduction processes at -1.19, -1.44, and -1.90 V vs Fc/Fc+, indicating effective electronic communication between the two porphyrin moieties.
knowledge_points.evidence: 12 underwent three quasi-reversible reductions at -1.19, -1.44, and -1.90 V ... The three one-electron reduction processes of 12 reflect distinct electronic communication over the two porphyrin moieties through the phosphole moiety.

knowledge_points.content: The precursor bis(pyrrolo)phosphole 7 is synthesized as a P=S derivative to ensure stability under ambient conditions, as the P(III) derivative is unstable.
knowledge_points.evidence: Whereas the P(III) derivative is unstable under ambient atmosphere, the P=S compound 7 is sufficiently stable to be used as the precursor.
